name: Placenta encapsulation
summary: Capsules, tinctures, prints and keepsakes, prepared with strict safety practices.
description: Placenta encapsulation, tinctures, prints and keepsakes in Bend and Central Oregon from a Certified Placenta Specialist. Pickup and delivery included.
intro: Whether you want capsules, a tincture, or a keepsake to honor your pregnancy, I offer placenta services with care, from pickup after your birth to delivery of your chosen preparation.

Some people find that placenta consumption supports their recovery. Scientific research is limited, so I always recommend talking with your healthcare provider first. Non-consumption options like prints and cord keepsakes are available too, including in times of loss.

items.title: Encapsulation
items.text: The placenta is steamed, dehydrated, ground into a powder and placed in easy-to-take capsules.

items.title: Powder
items.text: The dehydrated, ground placenta as a loose powder, to mix into food or smoothies.

items.title: Tincture
items.text: A portion of the placenta steeped in alcohol for extended use.

items.title: Prints and keepsakes
items.text: A placenta print made with natural, non-toxic methods, or a dried umbilical cord keepsake.

faqs.a: When properly handled and prepared it is generally considered safe for healthy individuals, but research is limited. Please talk with your healthcare provider before deciding.

faqs.q: How should I store my placenta until pickup?
faqs.a: Place it in a clean sealed container or double bag and refrigerate or keep it in a cooler within two to four hours of birth. I provide detailed instructions when you book.
In your third trimester or earlier. A deposit holds your spot.
Preparing and ingesting the placenta after delivery, most often through encapsulation, tinctures or powder. Many people choose it to support postpartum recovery.

Scientific research is limited. Many parents report more energy, mood support, help with milk supply and a smoother recovery. Please talk with your healthcare provider about whether it is right for you.
Most healthy people can, but some conditions may make it unsafe, such as infections during labor or placenta abnormalities. I am happy to help you think it through.

faqs.q: How long do capsules and powder last?
faqs.a: Stored in a cool, dry place, several months to a year. Some people freeze a portion for later.

faqs.q: How do I use a placenta tincture?
faqs.a: Typically in small doses, a few drops under the tongue or in a drink. Stored in a cool, dark place, a tincture keeps for years.

faqs.q: Are there risks to consuming raw placenta?
faqs.a: Yes. There is a higher risk of bacterial contamination with raw placenta than with encapsulation. Always consult your care provider first.
A keepsake made by pressing the placenta onto paper, which captures its "tree of life" shape.

faqs.q: Can I keep a keepsake and still encapsulate?
faqs.a: Yes. You can have a print, a cord keepsake or a tincture and still encapsulate the rest.
